correctness.rationale: Twenty four-point lines and their pair uniqueness are verified by two finite-field incidence constructions. Their basis counts (480 total, 90 through a point, 12 through a pair) give the exact incidence moment formula for all character supports. From this identity the first possible zero weight six and unique line-plus-transversal geometry with exactly 960 supports are proved without computational extrapolation. The accompanying standalone integer checker evaluates all 65,536 frequencies by both complete Walsh transform and the independent incidence formula, asserting the full absolute histogram, 6,150 zeros, exact rank 59,386, min positive magnitude four and endpoint projection numerator 2,232,436. The translation-averaging proof establishes optimality among all real or complex projections.

originality.rationale: An order-four affine plane has four-point lines and a sixteen-coordinate Boolean incidence group. The historical affine geometry text defines the relevant matroid and parameters but contains no positionwise Walsh spectrum, nullity 6150, 960 first-cancellation supports or projection constant. Comparable published signed-spectral results concern Steiner systems with three-point lines and binary projective matroids; they do not imply the specific sixteen-point affine computation. A separately calculated nine-point affine plane result has a different incidence dimension and line cardinality. Actual searches for exact parameters, equivalent signed transforms, line-intersection formulations and stronger covering theorems returned no dominating theorem; this is bounded originality, not global uniqueness.

value.rationale: The canonical four-element-field affine plane is the first non-ternary 16-point rank-three affine geometry, and the precise first-cancellation degree and geometry are motivated by low-degree signed incidence information. The 960-line-plus-transversal boundary exposes a nonlocal Fourier obstruction; the full rank and exact unrestricted endpoint projection constant quantify finite Fourier recovery and stability rather than recomputing the ordinary 480-base count. This is a natural complete finite classification with exact future benchmarking value, not a claimed arbitrary slice or unmotivated parameter.
